PHI.head: A big edge for the Flyers

VAN.head: The Flyers should be favored

story.head: Expect a grind
paras: The Flyers won the teams’ first meeting this season, 3-1 in Vancouver on Nov 9. The Canucks (6-20-1) lost 5-1 to Detroit on Wednesday, and the Flyers (9-12-6) lost 7-3 to Washington the same night. Going in, the Canucks are last in the NHL and the Flyers fifth in the Metropolitan (tied for 21st in the NHL).

The Canucks haven’t played well, but their record (.241) is worse than their play: their chances are worth about .340, and their goaltending has held them back. The Flyers’ record (.444) is about what their chances are worth.

The Canucks (lowest) and the Flyers (3rd lowest) both pick their shots. The Canucks have had shaky goaltending (32nd) and have a leaky penalty kill (32nd). Vancouver has allowed 4.41 goals a game, the most in the league. On the other side, the Flyers take away shots from the point (3rd lowest). Philadelphia has scored 2.59 goals a game, the fourth fewest in the league. Both teams play slow, low-event hockey, especially the Flyers (2nd lowest), so expect a tight one.

Brock Boeser (8 G / 20 A / 28 P in 27 GP) is carrying the Canucks’ offense, with eight points in his last five games. For the Flyers, Christian Dvorak (5 G / 11 A / 16 P in 27 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Trevor Zegras (5 G / 10 A / 15 P in 27 GP) isn’t far behind.
Leevi Meriläinen (4-11-1 / .885 SV% in 17 GS) is expected to start for Vancouver, and Dan Vladař (4-5-4 / .874 SV% in 13 GS) for Philadelphia.
At home, Rick Tocchet likes to send Foerster, Dvorak and Konecny out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against DeBrusk, Chytil and Boeser.

items.text: The Canucks have been without Elias Pettersson (#40) since Nov 19, and have had to make do without Thatcher Demko all season. Leevi Meriläinen is expected to start.
The Flyers are newly without Matvei Michkov.
With Elias Pettersson (#40) out, Brock Boeser took eight faceoffs in the Canucks’ last game. He had been taking about two a game.
Trevor Zegras has four goals on chances worth about 6.8 goals, well below what his finishing usually turns chances into. If the chances keep coming, so should the goals.
